html:
Sardinia is the second largest island in the Mediterranean, west of Italy. On the map from 1000 to 1715 it stands for the island's own medieval states and then the kingdom that Aragon and Spain ruled there.

After Byzantine rule faded in the 800s and 900s, the island ran itself as four small kingdoms called judicates, each under a judge: Cagliari, Arborea, Gallura and Logudoro. The sea republics of Pisa and Genoa fought for influence, trade and land on the island, as they did on neighbouring Corsica.

In 1297 the pope created a Kingdom of Sardinia and Corsica and granted it to the king of Aragon. The Aragonese invaded in 1323. Arborea resisted for almost a century. Its ruler Eleanor of Arborea issued the Carta de Logu, a law code in the Sardinian language that stayed in force until 1827. Arborea gave up in 1420.

Sardinia then spent three centuries as a poor, thinly peopled province of Aragon and Spain, ruled by viceroys. In the War of the Spanish Succession it passed to Austria, and in 1720 Austria swapped it with the House of Savoy for Sicily. The dukes of Savoy took the title King of Sardinia, so the island gave its name to the Kingdom of Sardinia that later united Italy.
sum: Sardinia is the second largest island in the Mediterranean, west of Italy. On the map from 1000 to 1715 it stands for the island's own medieval states and then the kingdom that Aragon and Spain ruled there.
